:::{#exr-zero-vector-practice}
#### Picking the zero vector with three entries from three candidates

A [zero vector](#def-zero-vector) has a number of entries as well as zero entries,
so $\vzero \in \reals^2$ and $\vzero \in \reals^3$ are different vectors.
Consider three candidates:

$$
\vecf{a} = \sbmat{0 \\ 0},
\qquad
\vecf{b} = \sbmat{0 \\ 0 \\ 0},
\qquad
\vecf{c} = \sbmat{0 \\ 1 \\ 0}.
$$

Which of the three candidates is the zero vector with $3$ entries?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

@def-zero-vector has two conditions:
$3$ entries,
and every entry equal to $0$.

:::

:::
